title: ALMA and VLBA views on the outflow associated with an O-type protostar in G26.50+0.28
question: How are jets and outflows associated with an O-type protostar candidate in G26.50+0.28 structured, precessing, rotating, and launched in the close vicinity of the protostar?

data.sensitivity: Continuum 1sigma = 0.3 mJy beam^-1; 13CO(2-1) and SiO(5-4) 1sigma <= 5.0 mJy beam^-1 per 1 km s^-1 channel

what.value: Maser parallax distance of 6.3+0.5/-0.4 kpc and detailed VLBA observation information

evidence.quote: Located at a maser parallax distance of 6.3$^{+0.5}_{-0.4}$ kpc (cite: 2021ApJS..253....1X), G26.50+0.28 (also known as IRAS 18360-0537)
G26.50+0.28 (also known as IRAS 18360-0537) has a far-Infrared luminosity of 1.2$\times$10$^5$ L$_{\odot}$ (Molinari et al. 1996).

what.value: SMA 1.3 mm continuum, 13CO(2-1), SiO(5-4), CH3OH, CH3CN, and CN observations, infall rate of 1.5 x 10^-3 M_sun yr^-1, central star mass of 12 M_sun, and systemic velocity of ~104 km s^-1

evidence.quote: Furthermore, CN spectra, also from the SMA, present typical inverse P-Cygni profiles that demonstrate infall motions of about 1.5$\times$10$^{-3}$ M$_{\rm \odot}$ yr$^{-1}$ (Qiu et al. 2012).
Then the derived mass of the central star $M_{\star}$ is about 15 M$_{\odot}$, which is consistent with the mass derived by (cite: 2012ApJ...756..170Q) of 12 M$_{\odot}$.
close to the systematic velocity ($\approx$104 $\hbox{${\rm km\,s}^{-1}$}$, derived from Gaussian fits of ALMA CH$_{3}$CN lines (cite: 2012ApJ...756..170Q))

recipe.goal: Calibrate, combine, and image multi-configuration ALMA continuum and line data
recipe.method: Run ALMA pipeline separately on 7m, C-4, and C-6 datasets, combine visibilities, subtract continuum with uvcontsub (order 1), and image continuum (MFS) and line cubes (1 km s^-1 channels over 70-140 km s^-1) using Briggs weighting (robust=0.5) and multiscale deconvolution.

recipe.goal: Measure MM1 disk/toroid geometry, scale height, kinematics, and central protostellar mass
recipe.method: Measure deconvolved major and minor axes of MM1 from 1.3 mm continuum, compute disk scale height H using the jet inclination, and derive central star mass from H, disk radius, and CH3OH line FWHM; examine velocity gradients in CH3OH and CH3CN moment-1 and position-velocity diagrams.
assumptions: Circular disk/toroid perpendicular to the jet with jet inclination i = 8 deg; distance = 6.3 kpc; 1.3 mm continuum dominated by dust

recipe.goal: Map outflow/jet morphology, fit jet precession, and test for jet rotation in ALMA line cubes
recipe.method: Construct velocity-integrated maps of 13CO(2-1) and SiO(5-4), fit a 2D projected sinusoidal precession model to the SiO(5-4) jet emission, and inspect the SiO(5-4) moment-1 map within a 2.0"-wide belt along the jet axis for transverse velocity gradients.
key_parameters: Jet belt width = 2.0" for SiO(5-4) moment-1 map
assumptions: Inclination i fixed to 8.0 deg; distance = 6.3 kpc; jet velocity ~ 30 km s^-1 (or ~ 200 km s^-1) to estimate precession period

recipe.goal: Calibrate 15-epoch VLBA water maser data, extract maser spot positions, and fit 3D proper motions and ring geometry
recipe.method: Calibrate and image 15 epochs of VLBA 22.235 GHz data using AIPS/ParselTongue with inverse phase-referencing on a reference maser spot; fit 2D Gaussians with AIPS task SAD; fit a 3D ellipse to the MC-1 ring to derive inclination; fit linear constant-velocity proper motions to 216 spots persisting >= 5 epochs.
assumptions: Reference maser spot is co-moving with systemic velocity (~104 km s^-1) and unaffected by outflow; MC-1 ring is a 3D circle perpendicular to the jet axis; maser flux is proportional to wind particle intensity

However, pixel size, line-free channel ranges, moment map velocity ranges, and the exact locus extraction method for the precession fit are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival ALMAGAL dataset (2019.1.00195.L) for a single target with short integration times; key ALMA results (MM1 deconvolved size, central star mass, jet P.A., outflow shell opening angle, and precession parameters) are quantitative and can be reproduced from the ALMA visibilities.
